prompt_text: What are the best vacation rentals in Santa Cruz County California and how do I pick one?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- There’s no single “best” rental — the right one depends on where in Santa Cruz County you want to be (beach town vs redwoods vs cliffside), how many people, whether you need pet‑friendly or kid gear, and your budget.  
- Popular places that consistently get top reviews: West Cliff/Wharf area (Santa Cruz city) for surf/boardwalk access; Capitola Village and Seacliff/Rio del Mar for classic beach cottages; Davenport and the coast north of Santa Cruz for dramatic cliffs and quiet; Aptos/Seacliff for family beaches and Seacliff State Beach; Santa Cruz Mountains (Ben Lomond/Boulder Creek) for redwood cabins and privacy.  

If you want, I can pull current listings for your dates — tell me travel dates, party size, budget, and priorities (oceanfront, pet, kids, work Wi‑Fi, parking, etc.).

How to pick the best vacation rental for you — checklist and recommendations
1. Decide the location by experience
   - Santa Cruz Wharf & West Cliff: walk to restaurants, beach, surf breaks, family attractions (Boardwalk). Good if you want nightlife and convenience.
   - Capitola Village: colorful seaside village, beach right there, easy for families and casual dining.
   - Seacliff / Rio del Mar / Aptos: calmer, family beaches, Seacliff has a pier/ship wreck to explore.
   - Davenport / North Coast: dramatic cliffside views, quieter, good for romantic getaways and photography.
   - Santa Cruz Mountains (Ben Lomond, Boulder Creek, Felton): redwood privacy, hiking, cabins with fireplaces — farther from beaches.
2. Filter by practical must-haves
   - Sleeps X people, number of bedrooms/beds and bathrooms
   - Parking (on-street vs dedicated spot — important in Capitola and Wharf)
   - Pet policy (many places are NOT pet-friendly)
   - Accessibility (few beachfront properties are stair-only)
   - Amenities: full kitchen, washer/dryer, dishwasher, outdoor space, hot tub, fireplace, AC/heat, Wi‑Fi (for remote work)
3. Read the reviews (especially the last 6–12 months)
   - Look for repeated comments about cleanliness, accurate photos, host responsiveness, parking, noise, and neighborhood safety.
4. Check house rules and restrictions
   - Many Santa Cruz area rentals ban parties, limit occupancy, and have quiet hours. Hosts often require a signed rental agreement.
5. Check cancellation, fees, and taxes
   - Watch cleaning fees, service fees, and refundable security deposit. Short‑term rental taxes and local occupancy taxes often get added.
6. Confirm logistics before booking
   - Ask about check‑in/check‑out, key pickup, surfboard storage, EV charging, and nearest grocery store.
7. Verify legal status and registration
   - Santa Cruz County and some cities require STR registration and limits. For long stays or business travel, prefer professionally managed properties (Vacasa, local vacation‑rental companies) or Superhosts with a lot of reviews.

Types of rentals and who they suit
- Oceanfront condo / house (Wharf, West Cliff, Capitola): best for beach access, views, walks. Good for couples and families who want convenience.
- Beach cottage (Capitola, Seacliff): cozy, charming, great for photos and families. Watch for stairs and small kitchens.
- Cliff/Coastal home (Davenport, Bonny Doon): dramatic scenery and privacy; not always good for easy beach access.
- Redwood cabin / mountain home (Ben Lomond, Felton): great for hiking, privacy, fireplaces — better for driving to beaches.
- Luxury estate (oceanfront or mountain): lots of space and amenities, high cost and often booking required months ahead.
- Budget condo/apartment (offside Santa Cruz neighborhoods): pragmatic option for short stays and easy access to town.

Neighborhood pros/cons quick guide
- West Cliff / Santa Cruz Wharf: pros — walk everywhere; cons — can be touristy and noisy in summer.
- Capitola Village: pros — iconic beach vibe, restaurants; cons — limited parking, expensive in season.
- Seacliff / Rio del Mar / Aptos: pros — family beaches, quieter; cons — less nightlife.
- Davenport / north coast: pros — secluded, scenic; cons — farther from shops/restaurants.
- Santa Cruz Mountains: pros — peaceful, redwoods; cons — drive time to coast, narrow mountain roads.

Money and timing tips
- Peak season: mid‑June through August — book 3–6+ months ahead. Prices surge and minimum stays often 3+ nights or weekly.
- Shoulder season (May, September–October): milder weather, fewer crowds, better deals.
- Winter: dramatic coast, lower prices, some properties close for repairs; check for storm closures.
- Typical nightly ranges (very approximate): budget condo $150–300, beach cottage $250–600, oceanfront/luxury $600–2,000+.

Safety, parking and access reminders
- Many coastal properties have stairs down to beaches; not ideal for mobility restrictions.
- Parking can be limited in Capitola Village and near the Wharf. Confirm number of parking spots.
- For surfers: check whether shore access requires walking across private property, if an outdoor shower exists, and if there’s secure board storage.
- Check for neighborhood restrictions on events/extra cars/noise — enforcement is common.

Where to search
- VRBO and Airbnb have the largest inventories. Vacasa and local agencies often manage better‑equipped properties and provide on‑call support. Use the map view and filter for your essentials (parking, pets, oceanfront).

Quick sample picks (by style) — examples of what to look for
- “Walk-to-Boardwalk” condo: 2BR, ocean views, Wi‑Fi, 1 dedicated parking spot — great for families visiting Santa Cruz Boardwalk.
- “Capitola Village cottage”: 1–3BR, steps to Capitola Beach, front porch, parking can be tight — great for romantic or small family stays.
- “Seacliff family home”: 3BR, yard, short walk to Seacliff State Beach, pet-friendly options exist.
- “Davenport cliff house”: 2BR, large windows and private deck, secluded — best for couples and photographers.
- “Ben Lomond redwood cabin”: 2–4BR, fireplace, hot tub, hiking out the door — ideal for groups wanting nature.

Final offer
If you want specific current recommendations, tell me:
- travel dates (or season), length of stay
- number of guests (adults, kids), pets?
- must‑have amenities (oceanfront, hot tub, kitchen, parking, baby gear, work Wi‑Fi)
- budget per night (or total)

I’ll search and give 6–8 well‑matched rental suggestions with pros/cons and booking tips.
